questions.q: What transformation engine does a Dataflow Gen2 use?
options: KQL, the query language covered in a later chapter
PySpark, exactly like a Fabric notebook
Power Query — the same engine behind Power BI's own data prep
T-SQL exclusively, with no other transformation option
questions.explain: Each transformation is a recorded step, shown as a readable list, rather than a line of code.

questions.q: What's the real difference between a Dataflow's steps and a notebook's PySpark code?
options: Notebooks cannot write to a lakehouse table, only Dataflows can
Steps use Power Query's own transformation language (M) with a click-based mental model; PySpark is real code with the DataFrame API
Dataflows can only read data, never transform it
They are exactly the same underlying technology, just different UI
questions.explain: This is a genuinely different mental model — describing what changes via steps, rather than writing code.

questions.q: Why would a Dataflow be a poor fit for this course's full-scale NYC Taxi trip data?
options: It needs casting/deduplication/window-function logic at millions of rows, which a real notebook with PySpark is better suited for than Dataflows
Dataflows only work with data already in Delta format
Dataflows cannot write to a lakehouse table at all
There's no real reason; Dataflows are always the better choice at any scale
questions.explain: Dataflows fit well for smaller, business-user-friendly transformations, not this scale or kind of logic.

questions.q: Where does a Dataflow's transformed output actually land?
options: It cannot write to any table; Dataflows are read-only
Only into a temporary in-memory cache with no persistent storage
Directly into a lakehouse or warehouse table, via its Data destination setting — the same Tables area from Lesson 4
Only into a separate, Dataflow-specific storage system inaccessible to other tools
questions.explain: From that point on, it's queryable by a notebook, a pipeline, or Power BI, exactly like any other lakehouse table.

questions.q: For what kind of task does this lesson suggest a Dataflow is a genuinely reasonable choice?
options: Row-level and column-level security definitions
Real-time streaming ingestion
The full NYC Taxi trip dataset at millions of rows
This course's small zones lookup table — a few hundred rows with simple column cleanup
questions.explain: This is the kind of cleanup a business user might already be comfortable doing without writing code.
